1. (Currently amended) A lamp comprised of an at least substantially hollow columnar body, a plurality of light emitting diodes disposed on said columnar body, a plurality of fins disposed on said columnar body, a base member disposed at a first end of the columnar body and providing a means for electrical connection, __an optic element overlapping at least one of said diodes__, and an electronics module disposed within the columnar body and in electrical communication with the base member.

2. (Previously presented) The lamp of claim 1 wherein a second end of said columnar body is open.

3. (Currently amended) The lamp of claim 1 __wherein said optic element is__ a light dispersing optic element overlapping said diodes.

4. (Previously presented) The lamp of claim 4 wherein said optic element includes a phosphor material.

5. (Currently amended) The lamp of claim 1 wherein said diodes are substantially evenly spaced radially around the columnar body __and said fins are substantially equally disposed between said diodes__.

6. (Cancelled)

7. (Currently amended) The lamp of claim 1 wherein said columnar body comprises one of a tetragon, pentagon, hexagon, heptagon, octagon, nonagon, decagon, hendecagon, or dodecagon in cross-section __and said optic element preferentially directs light substantially perpendicular to an elongated axis of the columnar body__.

8. (Previously presented) The lamp of claim 7 wherein at least one diode resides on each face of said columnar body.

9. (Previously presented) The lamp of claim 8 wherein one fin resides on each corner of said columnar body.

10. (Previously presented) The lamp of claim 9 wherein a single diode resides on each face.

11. (Currently amended) The lamp of claim 1 wherein said columnar body and said fins are comprised of a material having a thermal conductivity greater than 100 W/mK __and said electronics module comprises a printed circuit board including circuitry for converting AC to DC current__.

12. (Previously presented) The lamp of claim 9 including a single optic element is disposed between each adjacent fin over-lapping said diode.

13. (Currently amended) The lamp of claim 1 wherein said base member comprises an Edison screw base or a wedge base __and said electronics module comprises a printed circuit board including circuitry for converting AC to DC current__.

14. (Cancelled)

15. (Previously presented) The lamp of claim 3 wherein said optic element preferentially directs light substantially perpendicular to an elongated axis of the columnar body.

16. (Currently amended) A lamp comprising an elongated hollow polygonal body comprised of a material having a thermal conductivity greater than 100 W/mK, a fin extending radially from each corner of said body, a light emitting diode mounted to each side of said body, __an optic element overlapping at least one of said light emitting diodes__, a screw or wedge base connector closing a first end of said body, a second end of said body being open, an electronics module disposed within said body in electrical communication with said connector and said light emitting diodes, said lamp having a general A19 outline.

17. (Currently amended) A method of manufacturing a lamp comprising extruding an elongated hollow body, said body comprised of a material having a thermal conductivity greater than 100 W/mK, cutting said body to a predetermined length, attaching at least one light emitting diode to said body, __attaching an optic element overlapping at least one of said light emitting diodes__, and providing electrical circuitry suitable for powering said light emitting diode.

18. (Previously presented) The method of claim 17 wherein said material has a thermal conductivity greater than about 150 W/mK.

19. (Previously presented) The method of claim 17 wherein said body includes a plurality of integral radially extending fins.

20. (Previously presented) The method of claim 20 wherein said body has substantially straight side walls.
